builder-criteria.why: all 6 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why:
I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2 and 5 stay within what their lines say, but three checks ask for more:

- **Check 4:** The expect line says only that "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged". The PASS condition instead requires the whole file to be identical, via a fixed sha256 hash and `git diff --exit-code` against a base commit. That is a file-scope rule the words don't force.
- **Check 3 (D and E):** The words say only "error on stderr". PASS also requires that "the stderr line names missing.jsonl", which is stricter.
- **Check 6:** The words say "one PR". PASS requires "exactly one open PR", but the expect line doesn't mention the PR's state.

Each of these extra requirements should have gone under Advisory.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the repo's file list and against shell and jq syntax. Every file they name exists in the repo: packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js, src/index.js, test/cli.test.js, README.md and .github/workflows/test.yml. Root `npm test` runs `node --test` in each workspace, so it works. In Checks 1–3, each `T=$(mktemp -d) && printf ... && B=...; node "$B" ...; echo "exit=$?"` chain has valid quoting, redirections and `for` loops. Nested quotes such as `"stderr: $(cat "$T/err")"` are also valid. In Check 4, `git diff --exit-code <sha> HEAD -- path` and `sha256sum` are valid. I couldn't confirm that the fixed sha b74bddb… exists in the repo. It is presumably the base commit. In Check 6, the `gh api` jq filters are valid (`select((.body // "") | contains(...))`, string interpolation). The `<sha>` placeholder is explained in the text before it. The JavaScript the builder brief suggests, `readFileSync(0, 'utf8')`, is valid.

catches-traps.why: I checked all four must_catch items and the briefs handle each one. (1) Verifier Check 3 case D runs `"$T/missing.jsonl" "$T/bad.jsonl" "$T/good1.jsonl"` together and passes only if the output still shows the `$T/bad.jsonl:2`/`:4` lines, stderr names missing.jsonl, and exit=2. (2) Check 4 runs `git diff --exit-code b74bddb… HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` and expects `UNCHANGED`, so it compares against the base commit. (3) Builder step 5 says "Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md" with the multi-file usage, how `-` works and the exit codes. (4) Check 6 uses gh api to find the PR whose body contains the exact Closes line. It requires that PR's head sha to be the commit under check, reads that sha's check-runs, and requires `test` to be `completed success`.

avoids-must-not.why: Must_not item 2 holds: Checks 1–3 all run the bin with real files and stdin, so no behaviour line is passed just by reading the code. Item 1 fails. Line 4 only says "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged", but Check 4 asks for the whole file to match a fixed sha256 hash and to show no `git diff` at all. So any edit elsewhere in src/index.js fails the check even if lint stays the same, which in effect limits which files the PR may touch. The builder brief says the same thing: "do not touch ... src/index.js at all (not even whitespace)". Check 6 is also stricter than line 6: it requires "exactly one open PR", so a merged PR would fail, and the line asks only for one PR. Check 3 also requires that stderr names missing.jsonl, which the line does not ask for.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's PASS/FAIL conditions and probes. Two of the verifier's specific conditions show up in the builder brief. First, step 3 says "so output for several files equals the concatenation of single-file runs". That is Check 1's PASS condition ("multi-file output equals the concatenation of single-file runs", tested with diff → SAME), not just the expect line's "as for one file before". Second, step 4's missing-file test asks that "a bad file named after the missing one is still reported on stdout" and that "stderr names the missing file". This copies Check 3 D's probe and PASS condition (missing file first, then bad.jsonl lines still on stdout, stderr names missing.jsonl). The rest of the builder brief stays within what's allowed: restating the expect lines, running npm test, and writing its own tests. But these overlaps give the builder the checker's methods, so the criterion fails.
